title: Nvidia tightens tracking of AI GPUs in Southeast Asia as Chinese chip smuggling draws scrutiny, report claims
content: Nvidia is requiring Southeast Asian cloud providers seeking Nvidia Cloud Partner status to enroll in its Fleet Intelligence tracking program, giving the chipmaker greater visibility into where its AI GPUs are deployed. The move comes as Washington increases pressure over suspected chip smuggling into China, with investigations involving Megaspeed International and Super Micro highlighting the challenges of enforcing U.S. export restrictions

title: Six pallets of Nvidia GPUs worth $11.4 million stolen in California cargo heist
content: The latest incident comes amid growing concerns over GPU theft, with experts warning that advanced Nvidia chips can command significantly higher prices abroad and could end up in black-market channels.

title: Nvidia wants to repurpose over 130 old telco buildings as tiny data centers, report claims
content: Brightspeed has over 130 facilities located across the U.S., with Nvidia estimating that they could produce up to 1GW of compute capacity.

title: Tesla unveils AI accelerator roadmap, adopts new 'SI' branding in 'Super Intelligence' push
content: Tesla is ramping up its custom silicon ambitions with training-oriented Dojo D3 that can eventually go to orbital data centers and massive SI6 inference accelerator.

title: Intel’s next-gen Nova Lake needs new motherboards — what we expect from Nova Point and Z990, Z970, and B960 chipsets

title: Score a huge $600 saving on this RTX 5070 Ti gaming laptop from HP, now under $2,100
content: Save $600 on this customizable RTX 5070 Ti HP Omen Max 16 gaming laptop with 16GB DDR5, 512GB SSD, and a 16-inch display.

title: Gelsinger-backed Nagare Labs’ Z2RAM promises SRAM speed at DRAM density
content: Georgia Tech spinout Nagare Labs, backed by Playground Global, unveils Z2RAM, a capacitorless memory to stack on AI accelerators.

title: US lawmakers request briefing with Nvidia's Jensen Huang on dealings with Megaspeed executive
content: Three US lawmakers asked Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to attend a closed-door meeting to discuss his interactions with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang. The request followed recent reports alleging that Alice Huang had fed intelligence to the Chinese government and had developed a "close relationship" with Jensen Huang.

title: Commentary: US governors target AI data centers as Taiwan firms await Nvidia outlook
content: Following the 2026 US gubernatorial elections, four states that host major AI data centers—Texas, Ohio, Georgia, and Pennsylvania—could impose tighter controls on new projects after Democratic candidates won or secured reelection, according to Bloomberg. Taiwan suppliers are watching closely as some projects could be paused, while Nvidia's upcoming earnings call is expected to provide clues on AI infrastructure demand.

title: Moonshot AI reportedly seeking access to Nvidia GPUs through European neoclouds
content: Moonshot AI, a leading Chinese model developer, is reportedly seeking remote access to Nvidia chips held in Europe. With sales of advanced US chips to China limited, the move would exploit a loophole in American law that currently does not restrict cloud service providers (CSPs) from selling compute to Chinese companies.

title: YMTC targets up to 70% Chinese tools for new NAND fab
content: China's Yangtze Memory Technologies (YMTC) plans to source as much as 70% of the manufacturing equipment for its fourth NAND flash factory from domestic suppliers, a substantial increase over the share at its existing operations as the company expands into advanced memory for AI and data centers.

title: Democrats constrain Trump as scarce AI capacity benefits CSPs
content: Democrats swept the US midterm elections, reshaping the global technology and industrial landscape. Their victories in key gubernatorial races, including in Texas and Georgia, have raised concerns about AI infrastructure expansion after some winning candidates explicitly pledged to pause data-center development.

title: Wistron ITS reports record third-quarter profit as AI and semiconductor focus accelerates
content: Wistron ITS reported record gross profit, operating profit, net income, and earnings per share in the third quarter of 2026, as stronger revenue and improved operating efficiency supported continued expansion in AI and semiconductor services. Consolidated revenue reached NT$3.752 billion (approx. US$114.1 million), up 3.5% quarter-over-quarter and 25.6% year-over-year.

title: US election backlash reshapes AI data center expansion strategies
content: Companies at the forefront of the AI infrastructure buildout in the US are taking different approaches following the results of this week's midterm elections, which saw a nationwide backlash against data center construction. OpenAI pledged to prevent resource impacts on communities, while Nvidia is turning toward retrofitting small existing facilities.

title: Taiwan science park debt tops NT$160 billion as NSTC targets faster repayment
content: Debt held by Taiwan's science park operating funds reached NT$163.54 billion (approx. US$4.97 billion) as of the end of September 2026, while the National Science and Technology Council (NSTC) remains confident that rising operating cash flow will accelerate repayment. The government continues to develop and expand science parks to meet industry demand, including new sites and expansions across Taiwan.

title: Tencent launches Hy4 model to boost visual reasoning, AI safety
content: Tencent has launched its next-generation artificial intelligence (AI) model, Hy4, adding visual understanding for the first time and limiting cybersecurity training data to reduce the risk of misuse in cyberattacks and harmful biological research.

title: Qualcomm validates HBC memory architecture, targets AI250 samples in 1H27
content: Qualcomm has completed initial hardware validation of its high-bandwidth compute (HBC) memory architecture, which will form a key part of its next-generation Dragonfly data-center AI accelerators. The company aims to deliver a lower-cost, more energy-efficient alternative to sixth-generation high-bandwidth memory (HBM4) for AI inference workloads requiring high bandwidth and large buffers.

title: EOI posts record nine-month results, readies Mexico plant for 4Q26 production
content: Excellence Opto (EOI), a major automotive LED light-source supplier, posted record revenue and profit for the first nine months as product-mix optimization, supply-chain efficiencies and high global capacity utilization lifted results. The company is also preparing to begin mass production at its Mexico plant in the fourth quarter and to develop SiPh optical communication module samples by 2027.

title: LX Semicon posts first quarterly operating loss since IPO
content: South Korean chip designer LX Semicon posted its first quarterly operating loss since going public in 2010, as weak demand for display chips and pricing pressure from electronics manufacturers weighed on earnings. The company also nominated a new CEO to lead its turnaround efforts.

title: TV panel makers hold prices firm in November despite fading demand, with supply cuts proving crucial
content: The global TV panel market entered a period of fragile equilibrium in November 2026 following the end of peak-season inventory replenishment. Although TV brands have become more cautious in procurement, panel manufacturers are adjusting production at advanced-generation LCD fabs to stabilize prices, with rising upstream material costs reinforcing their reluctance to offer discounts.

title: China's NSIG sees silicon wafer prices rebound, but profitability remains elusive
content: National Silicon Industry Group (NSIG) expects to complete its expansion to 1.2 million 300mm silicon wafers per month by the end of 2026, positioning the Chinese semiconductor materials supplier to benefit from recovering wafer prices and growing demand for silicon-on-insulator (SOI) substrates used in silicon photonics (SiPh).

title: China's chip equipment makers ride record AI orders into 2027, but new challenges lie ahead
content: Chinese semiconductor equipment makers report record orders extending into 2027, with AI-driven investment in advanced memory, logic chips and packaging strengthening demand for domestic manufacturing tools. The expansion is benefiting suppliers across etching, thin-film deposition, cleaning and electroplating, although component delivery constraints could delay the conversion of orders into revenue.
